summary: Joseph Mansion worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at Ghent University (1894–1899) and studied under Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served as chargé de cours (1904) and eo. Professor (1910) at the University of Liège.
Joseph Margolis was a philosopher who earned his M.A. from Columbia University (~1947–1950). In 1991, he held the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University.

Joseph A. Marino is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed M.A. degrees at Ohio State University and the University of Washington, studying under Collett Cox and Richard G. Salomon. He became Assistant Professor at the University of Washington in 2020.

Joseph Masson was an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate from KU Leuven in 1942. He held posts at Institut de Philosophie et Lettres Saint-Robert Bellarmin, the University of Namur, and the Pontifical Gregorian University (1958).
Joseph Menrad was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Munich. From 1921 to 1926, he served as school director at Willibald-Gymnasium.

Joseph Merkel was an Indologist who taught Franz Bopp. He served as a teacher at Karls-Universität Aschaffenburg (1810), a professor at Gymnasium Aschaffenburg (1818), and Hofbibliothekar at Hofbibliothek Aschaffenburg (1828).

Joseph Mullens worked in religious studies and Indology, studying at Coward College, Williams College, the University of Edinburgh, and the University of London. In 1865, he was appointed Foreign Secretary for the London Missionary Society.

Joseph Nadin Rawson worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Jesus College, Oxford, under Arthur Anthony Macdonell and J. N. Farquhar. He was Professor at Serampore College (~1913–1938) and a Fellow at the University of Calcutta.

Joseph Needham was a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. Educated at Cambridge, he served as Fellow and Master at Gonville and Caius College, Reader in Biochemistry at Cambridge (~1933–1966), and Director of the Needham Research Institute (~1976–1990).
Joseph Peet was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington, in 1829 and later served as Principal of CMS College Kottayam (~1833–1838).

Joseph Prabhu is a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who studied under John N. Findlay, Bernard Williams, and Alasdair MacIntyre. He held an Associate Professorship at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989).

Joseph Ratzinger was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Munich and Ducal Georgianum. He held academic posts at the universities of Munich (1958–1959), Bonn (1959–1963), Münster (1963–1966), Tübingen (~1966–1969), and Regensburg (~1969–1977).

Joseph Rock worked in sinology and tibetology. He held appointments at the Mid-Pacific Institute, Mills College, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, the USDA, the Army Map Service, and the Harvard-Yenching Institute (1946–1949).
Joseph Rupp was an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich. From 1850 to 1882, he served as a gymnasium professor at Dom-Gymnasium Freising.
Joseph S. Alter is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. He is attested as a Professor at the University of Pittsburgh in 2008.

Joseph T. O'Connell was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Holy Cross and Harvard (Ph.D.). He taught at the University of St. Michael's College and the University of Toronto (1968–2000), also teaching at Oxford, Visva-Bharati, and Dhaka.

Joseph Tiefenthaler was an Indologist and historian who served as a Jesuit missionary from 1729 to 1773. He worked as a teacher at Agra Jesuit College (~1744–1747) and later served as Rector of the Jesuit High School of Agra.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied under Silvestre de Sacy. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, INALCO, and served as President of the Société Asiatique (1847–1867).

Linguist Joseph Vendryes studied under Meillet, Henry, Lévi, and Thurneysen. He held a professorship in linguistics at the University of Paris (1923–1946) and taught at the École Normale Supérieure (1920–1936) and École Pratique des Hautes Études (1926–1952).

Joseph Virgil Grohmann was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Charles University, studying under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He later served as Professor at Prager Handelsakademie (1856–1863) and Director at Leitmeritzer Oberrealschule (1866).
